transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-30
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Blackstone Bio ML Eng), Tomás Ruiz (Blackstone Platform), Priya Nair (Blackstone CTO)

Auto-generated Summary (may be rough): Mid-pilot weekly check-in. Reviewed throughput and p95/p99 latency deltas vs incumbent. Agreed to move routing thresholds to favor Redwood for read-heavy traffic, requested dedicated slot pricing, and plan to run a baseline replay with updated prompts.

Shared artifacts referenced: https://redwood.s3/bench-results-blackstone-week3.csv (bench-results.csv) | routing-playbook.md (short notes in chat) | security-one-pager.pdf (sent previously)

Topics:
- Week 3 benchmark readout vs {IncumbentAI}
- Route decision: latency-sensitive vs cost-sensitive buckets
- Quantization and tokenization differences affecting p99
- Next steps: dedicated slot request, SOW, security docs handoff

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: All right, hi everyone. Thanks for joining, well do a quick 40 minute readout plus Q&A. Lara? sorry Lena, you there?
[00:12] Lena Ortiz: Yeah hi, sorry had a quick laptop swap. Can you share the top-line numbers first, like p50/p95/p99 vs the incumbent?
[00:18] Ravi Patel: Sure, I put the spreadsheet in the chat. Top-line: for the 512-token average prompt, Redwood p50 is 42ms, p95 is 180ms, p99 is 420ms. IncumbentAI p50 was 38ms, p95 250ms, p99 610ms on their reserved cluster snapshot. So we are faster at the tail by quite a bit.
[00:45] Speaker 1 (maybe Maya): Wait you said incumbent p95 250, that seems higher than our p95, right?
[00:48] Ravi Patel: Yeah so they have lower median but much worse tail, probably from their batching and queuing behaviour. Our continuous batching + prefix cache reduced the p99 for the workload.
[01:10] Tomás Ruiz: Is the traffic mix identical? I mean, we replayed our prod trace but theres an open question about token distribution, some of our calls have 1.2k tokens.
[01:25] Ravi Patel: Good point. The week3 replay included the long-tail requests; when we clamp to 256 tokens the p99 moves to 300ms roughly. The heavy tails push the 1.2k bucket to 800-1,100ms on both vendors but ours still kept fewer spikes.
[01:48] Priya Nair: Cost comparison? We care about unit cost per 1k tokens on steady throughput and also peak cost when burst happens.
[02:00] Maya Chen: We ran cost-normalized numbers. For steady-state 500rps mix, Redwood unit cost is about 0.009 per 1k tokens after autoscaling and cache savings, IncumbentAI was ~0.011 with their default policy. But using their spot instances decreased cost but increased p99s.
[02:25] Lena Ortiz: Hmm, so Redwood wins on tail and slightly on cost. Can you explain the tradeoff if we push for lower latency? Would that spike cost?
[02:35] Ravi Patel: If we push aggressive latency SLOs (reduce batching, smaller max batch sizes), throughput drops and cost per token increases ~15-25% for the same throughput target. Alternatively, we can use quantized model variant for lower GPU utilization which keeps costs down but sometimes increases p99 by 30-60ms depending on prompt shape.
[03:05] Tomás Ruiz: Any difference in hallucination/quality with quantized variant? Because QA flagged some earlier outputs as slightly terser.
[03:12] Ravi Patel: We did evaluations on the prompt set you sent. For most of your scaffolded prompts differences were minimal, there were edge cases in long context completions where word-choice changed. We logged those in the evals doc. If quality is critical for specific flows, we recommend mixed routing: quantized for majority, full-fp model for fidelity-critical routes.
[03:40] Maya Chen: This is where routing decisions help. We propose marking two route buckets: latency-sensitive (chat, short completion) and fidelity-sensitive (long completions, code gen). The routing-playbook we shared contains thresholds.
[04:00] Lena Ortiz: Can you walk through thresholds? Last week we had a cusp where 1200ms requests got pulled into the latency bucket and then hit fallback; we lost a small percentage of calls.
[04:18] Ravi Patel: Right. Current proposed thresholds: target p95 < 250ms for latency bucket, fallback to lower-cap model after 900ms cumulative generation wait, and automatic fallback policy to our dedicated backup region in case of sustained queueing. We can tune those numbers; the tradeoff is you might see small quality change when fallback triggers.
[04:42] Priya Nair: About that backup region fallback - what about data residency? Some of our PHI-mapped traffic must remain in region eu-west-1. Does the fallback respect that?
[04:55] Maya Chen: Yes, we honor region and data residency. Our routing policy can be constrained by region tags. Fallback will be to a compatible model in the same region or to your dedicated capacity if you have it set up.
[05:12] Tomás Ruiz: Ok good. On the numbers you posted, can you explain one oddity: our internal baseline replay shows IncumbentAI had fewer timeouts but more long tails. Why fewer timeouts?
[05:24] Ravi Patel: They have a longer overall request timeout and more aggressive queuing so short requests get through but when queue backs up long-tail keeps waiting; we observed they drop fewer requests but run much higher latency until they hit hard limits. Redwood's approach prefers keeping latency lower with preemptive fallback, which can look like more early timeouts but fewer prolonged tails.
[05:50] Lena Ortiz: That might explain some user complaints. Better to surface an early degraded answer quickly than delay 15s.
[05:56] Maya Chen: Exactly. Our preference is graceful degradation rather than long waits.
[06:03] Speaker 2 (customer): Question on dedicated slots: what's the minimum commitment and how does autoscale burst work with that?
[06:12] Maya Chen: Minimum reserved slot is 2xA100-equivalent slots for the pilot. We can size to your observed peak and allow burst to shared fleet with a soft cap. Pricing and SOW draft Ill send after this call.
[06:25] Lena Ortiz: Can you quantify expected p99 improvement with dedicated capacity?
[06:30] Ravi Patel: In internal tests, moving the pilot onto Dedicated with pinned capacity reduced observed p99 by ~20-35% on heavy-token workloads because it avoids cross-tenant interference and gives us more headroom for batching tuning. Expect p95 improvement as well. But unit cost per token will go up given reserved compute.
[06:52] Priya Nair: Security checklist - are we covered for SOC2 evidence and audit logs? We need KMS integration details for key management.
[07:02] Maya Chen: Yes, we provided security-one-pager.pdf last week and I'll push the KMS integration doc to you after. We support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for Private deployments; for Hosted we offer envelope encryption with audit logs.
[07:18] Tomás Ruiz: Could you re-share the log retention options? We need 12 months for certain endpoints.
[07:23] Maya Chen: We support configurable retention up to 24 months for enterprise tiers; we can enable 12 months for your pilot if needed.
[07:31] Lena Ortiz: Ok, back to tuning. Ravi, what routing config did you change after last week's incident?
[07:36] Ravi Patel: We lowered max batch size from 64 to 48 for the latency bucket and tightened the per-worker queue window from 200ms to 120ms. That reduced p99 spikes but cost increased slightly. I posted the before/after CSV in the chat.
[07:53] Lena Ortiz: I see the CSV. The number of tokens/sec stayed similar but p99 drops by about 120ms. Good. Can we run that config under a 10k synthetic concurrency test?
[08:05] Ravi Patel: Yes, thats the plan for early next week. Well run 10k replay with your traffic profiles and compare aggregated metrics.
[08:12] Speaker 3 (Priya): Any special notes for loadgen? We have a nightly job that spikes at 18:00 local - should we try to emulate that?
[08:19] Ravi Patel: Please include spikes, bins for 1.2k token flows, and a separate fidelity route load. We'll attach the load script.
[08:28] Maya Chen: Also, want to call out an interesting find: the incumbent uses larger batch windows leading to better median but worse tail. For your interactive flows that matters.
[08:40] Tomás Ruiz: Understood. For the SLO, is there a recommended p95 target to be competitive?
[08:46] Ravi Patel: Recommend p95 < 220ms for chat, p95 < 500ms for long completions. Those are achievable with the current routing and a small dedicated slot.
[08:59] Lena Ortiz: Let's talk timeline. We want decision on provider by 2026-06-10, run final replay by 06-04, and finalize SOW by 06-08. Is that feasible?
[09:10] Maya Chen: Yes. For us we need to provision a dedicated slot once SOW is signed, that can take 3-5 business days.
[09:19] Priya Nair: One more: any regression risk from quantized variants? We are particularly sensitive for medical summarization flows.
[09:27] Ravi Patel: There is slight risk for long summarization where nuance matters. Our recommendation is hybrid routing and additional eval tests focusing on those flows.
[09:35] Maya Chen: Action items recap (quick): Ravi to deploy the tweaked routing and run 10k test; Maya to send pricing and SOW and security/KMS docs; Lena to run baseline replay and upload bench-results.csv; all to reconvene next Tuesday.
[09:52] Lena Ortiz: Sounds good. Also would like to add a micro-benchmark for tokenization differences; sometimes our pre-tokenization increased token counts which affects unit cost.
[10:02] Ravi Patel: Well include a tokenization report as part of bench results.
[10:10] Priya Nair: Cool. One last Q: Can we get a short note explaining fallback behavior in plain language for our legal team? They asked for clear failure modes.
[10:20] Maya Chen: Yep, well produce a one-page failure-mode summary and send it with the SOW.
[10:28] Maya Chen: All right that's it from us, thanks everyone.
[10:31] Tomás Ruiz: Thanks.
[10:33] Lena Ortiz: Thanks, see you next week.

End of recording.
